answer: Shale-seismic attestation: $140 per fake. Each identity owns one sensor sunk in a shale borehole; once an epoch the verifier fires a surface thump at an unannounced second and the sensor must report the ripple's arrival time within 40 ms, plus a photo of the dust plume rising within 10 s. A copied trace fails because shale layers bend each ripple differently, so one borehole's timing never matches another's. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 boreholes and $140,000; a farm cannot share geology. Limit: a rich farm can drill real holes, but each still costs the full $140.
